basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 5.' and it opens 'Vers. 5. Simeon et Levi, vasa iniquitatis bellantia. Hi duo fratres Dinae fuerunt, qui ob'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 5. Simeon et Levi, vasa iniquitatis bellantia. Hi duo fratres Dinae fuerunt, qui ob stuprum sororis saeviendo foederatam civitatem subverterunt caesis habitatoribus. Hos vocat vasa iniquitatis bellantia, id est instrumenta iniquitatis. In consilio eorum non veniet anima mea. His verbis ostendit non esse suae voluntatis ut Hemor et Sichem innocentes cum caeteris occiderentur. Non sit anima, id est voluntas et consilium.
